conventions.convention: The countable-state transition kernel is iterated from n = 0 with K^0 the identity, so p^(0)(x,y) is 1 exactly when x = y; rows of every iterate sum to 1.
The hitting time T_A includes time 0, the return time T_x^+ starts at n = 1, and N_x counts visits starting at n = 0.

Recurrence and transience are defined for the specified law started at x, by whether the strictly positive return time is finite with probability 1 or with probability less than 1; no simultaneous selection of laws for every state is asserted.

The discrete Green kernel is the extended nonnegative sum over n ≥ 0 and need not be finite; its expectation identity is asserted for a specified chain law under the stated Axiom of Choice assumption.

The planar canonical Green kernel is defined on a proper plane domain as the pointwise least nonnegative harmonic candidate with logarithmic coefficient exactly 1; zero boundary limit is required only at regular boundary points.
The planar PDE normalization is -Δ_z g = 2πδ at the pole, matching the source kernel Φ_2(z) = -(1/(2π)) log|z|; the cross-group source states Countable Choice and n ≥ 2.

Harmonic measure at z is a Radon Borel probability on the compact boundary representing the Perron extension for every real continuous boundary datum, and is defined here only for bounded regular plane domains.
Nevanlinna counts use closed discs with multiplicities and regularize the central divisor by n(0,a;f) log r; the characteristic is T = m(r,∞;f) + N(r,∞;f) with the normalized chordal distance.
The order and lower order use log T(r,f) / log r only for sufficiently large r > 1 with T(r,f) > 1; constant finite maps are assigned order and lower order 0.

load_bearing.statement: For meromorphic f on C not identically infinity and target a with f not identically a, N(r,a;f) = n(0,a;f) log r + integral from 0 to r of (n(t,a;f)-n(0,a;f))/t; the proximity is the circular mean of log(1/δ(f,a)), and T(r,f) = m(r,infinity;f) + N(r,infinity;f).

Assume AC. For a time-homogeneous Markov chain on an at most countable state space E, a fixed x and specified law with X_0 = x, and N_x counting visits including time 0: x is recurrent iff P_x(N_x = infinity) = 1 iff the sum over n ≥ 0 of p^(n)(x,x) diverges.

Assume Countable Choice. For bounded complex domain Ω and a ∈ Ω, g_Ω(z,a) = -log|z-a| - H_ba(z) is the canonical positive Green kernel: it is harmonic off a, has a harmonic corrector across a, is strictly positive and bounded away from the pole, tends to 0 at every regular boundary point, and satisfies -Δ_z T_g = 2πδ_a distributionally. No boundary value is prescribed at irregular boundary points.

Assume Dependent Choice. For each bounded regular plane domain Ω and z ∈ Ω there is exactly one Radon Borel probability ω_Ω^z on ∂Ω representing H_φ(z) for every real continuous φ; this integral is the unique continuous extension to the closure that is harmonic on Ω and agrees with φ on the boundary.

For nonconstant meromorphic f on C and a ∈ Ĉ, for every r > 0, m(r,a;f) + N(r,a;f) = T(r,f) + C(f,a); C(f,infinity)=0, and for finite a with first nonzero Laurent coefficient c_a at the centre, C(f,a) = (1/2) log(1+|a|²) - log|c_a|.

For meromorphic f,g on C, T(r,fg) ≤ T(r,f)+T(r,g)+O(1) and T(r,f+g) ≤ T(r,f)+T(r,g)+O(1) as r tends to infinity; if f is not identically zero, T(r,1/f)=T(r,f)+O_f(1); and for fixed rational R of degree d ≥ 1 and nonconstant meromorphic f, T(r,R(f))=dT(r,f)+O_(R,f)(1). Degree-zero rational maps give bounded characteristic after composition.

Assume Dependent Choice and bounded regular Ω. For every Borel E ⊆ ∂Ω, z ↦ ω_Ω^z(E) is harmonic and takes values in [0,1], and ω_Ω^z is countably additive in E; if Ω₁ ⊆ Ω₂ are bounded regular domains and E is Borel in their common boundary, then ω_Ω₁^z(E) ≤ ω_Ω₂^z(E) for z ∈ Ω₁.

Assume Dependent Choice and a bounded C¹ regular plane domain Ω. For real u ∈ C²(Ω) ∩ C¹(cl Ω) with bounded Δu, u(z) is the harmonic-measure boundary integral minus (1/(2π))∫_Ω g_Ω(z,y)Δu(y)dA(y), with both integrals absolutely finite. If ∂Ω is real analytic under the stated local curve hypothesis, dω_Ω^z = -(1/(2π)) ∂_ν g_Ω(z,ξ) ds; it makes no claim of pointwise Poisson density for arbitrary continuous data.

published_dependencies.used_for: The reciprocal-Gamma product used in the zero and growth estimates in ex-nevanlinna-characteristic-of-reciprocal-gamma.
The sectorial asymptotic used to obtain a lower growth bound for reciprocal Gamma.
The simple poles of Gamma at nonpositive integers, hence the zero locations and multiplicities of its reciprocal.
The existence of a finite zero of the denominator polynomial in the fixed rational composition argument.
Coefficient bounds used in the entire-function order comparison and rationality characterization.
Taylor expansions of entire functions used to compare maximum-modulus order and prove rationality from logarithmic characteristic.
Selecting the first integer radius at which the pole count reaches a chosen threshold in the rationality proof.
Matching poles and pole orders under the target Möbius transform and when cancelling the finite pole divisor.
Local zero multiplicities in the tangent continuation and target Möbius transform examples.
Holomorphy and derivative of the exponential composite used to identify the tangent example.
Showing the zeros that define tangent poles are isolated.

concerns.concern: Proof step 1.3 takes a continuous majorant φ₂ ≥ 1_K and then asserts its harmonic extension u₂ ≥ 0. The majorant condition does not require φ₂ to be nonnegative away from K, so the maximum principle does not imply that assertion. Restrict the majorants to nonnegative continuous functions; the cutoff constructed in step 1.4 is already nonnegative and supplies the required approximation.

seams_checked.note: The cited Green uniqueness item uses the fundamental-solution formula under Countable Choice and n ≥ 2, matching the source definition's assumptions and dimension-dependent constants. The source fixes Φ₂ = -(1/(2π)) log|x| and the higher-dimensional positive kernel; the citing text preserves the stated normalization.
